# go.build compiles a pattern or a list of them, reruns only when a matching
# package changes, and tracks the file `-o` in `flags` writes as an output
# that the cache restores.
[!exec:go] skip

bit
stdout 'all ▶ go build \./\.\.\.'
stdout 'listed ▶ go build \./a \./b'
stdout 'archive ▶ go build -o build/a\.a \./a'
exists build/a.a

cp c.go.changed c/c.go
bit
stdout 'all ▶ go build \./\.\.\. \(''c/c\.go'' changed\)'
! stdout 'listed ▶'
! stdout 'archive ▶'

# A broken package fails the targets that compile it.
cp b.go.broken b/b.go
! bit
stdout 'listed ✘'
stdout 'all ✘'
! stdout 'archive ✘'

cp b.go.fixed b/b.go
bit

rm build
bit
stdout 'archive │ restore build/a\.a'
exists build/a.a

# Cleaning removes the files `-o` wrote. Into a directory, `go build` writes
# only the main packages' executables, so the rest of it stays.
exists bin/tool bin/keep
bit --clean
! exists build/a.a
! exists bin/tool
exists bin/keep

-- BUILD.bit --
all = go.build {
  package = "./..."
}

listed = go.build {
  package = ["./a", "./b"]
}

archive = go.build {
  package = "./a"
  flags   = ["-o", "build/a.a"]
}

tools = go.build {
  package = ["./a", "./cmd/tool"]
  flags   = ["-o", "bin/"]
}
-- bin/keep --
-- cmd/tool/main.go --
package main

func main() {}
-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.22
-- a/a.go --
package a

func A() int { return 1 }
-- b/b.go --
package b

func B() int { return 2 }
-- b.go.broken --
package b

func B() int { return "two" }
-- b.go.fixed --
package b

func B() int { return 3 }
-- c/c.go --
package c
-- c.go.changed --
package c

const C = 1
